spatial_claims.claim: G lies on AD produced beyond D, giving collinear order A-D-G on a line
E is the midpoint of DG, giving collinear order D-E-G
F lies on segment AG such that rect(AF,FG) = sq(EG), giving collinear order A-F-G
U is cut at V to produce remainder W, a segment subtraction on a line

configuration_map: All constructed points lie on a single line or are abstract magnitudes. G lies beyond D on the extension of AD. E is the midpoint of segment DG. F lies on segment AG determined by the area condition rect(AF,FG) = sq(EG). LP and Q are constructed as abstract magnitudes (side of a square, fourth proportional). U and V are just LP and Q relabeled as greater and lesser. W is the remainder when V is cut from U. No complex spatial configuration exists — the proof operates entirely through commensurability relations and algebraic area identities.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic/proportional, dealing with commensurability relations between magnitudes and algebraic identities for rectangles and squares (II.1, II.4, II.7). All spatial claims are trivial collinear point placements on line segments. There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, no ray ordering claims, no circle arguments, and no triangle configuration claims. This is characteristic of Book 10 irrational magnitude proofs.
